description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review), Pass 4 of the ignored-tests audit (#993).
PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

REPRO (scratch/p50-stat-errno-only.pl):

    $! = 0; my @s = stat("/no/such/path/xyz");
    printf "stat: n=%d errno=[%s]\n", scalar(@s), ($! ? "$!" : "(0)");
    $! = 0; my $e = -e "/no/such/path/xyz";
    printf "-e:   errno=[%s]\n", ($! ? "$!" : "(0)");
    open(my $fh, '<', '/etc/passwd') or die; close $fh;
    $! = 0; my @b = stat($fh);
    printf "closed fh: n=%d errno=[%s]\n", scalar(@b), ($! ? "$!" : "(0)");

  perl 5.40.3:  stat errno=No such file or directory
                -e   errno=No such file or directory
                closed fh: n=0 errno=Bad file descriptor
  PCL:          stat errno=No such file or directory      <-- correct
                -e   errno=(0)                            <-- WRONG, errno untouched
                closed fh: n=0 errno=No such file or directory  <-- WRONG, want EBADF

TWO FACTS, one file:
  (a) `stat` on a missing PATH sets `$!` correctly, but a FILETEST on the same
      path does not touch it.  So `-e $f or die "cannot see $f: $!"` prints
      whatever errno happened to hold -- a stale value, or nothing.
  (b) An operation on a CLOSED handle reports ENOENT instead of EBADF.  perl
      distinguishes "the path is not there" from "that is not a usable
      descriptor", and code that branches on `$!{ENOENT}` vs `$!{EBADF}` takes
      the wrong branch.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: t/op/stat_errors.t, the VALUE half -- the file's 333
failing rows are `error from -X HANDLE` (311) and `result of stat HANDLE` (22)
in the s464ay t/op run.  They cannot be counted until **#1032** is fixed: the
file is written with BAREWORD handles, which crash the program before these
rows run.  Fix #1032 first, re-measure, then this.

RELATED: **#403** already owns the neighbouring claim that a filetest's FALSE
should be a DEFINED `""` when the stat succeeded (the 22 `result of` rows are
that family).  #403's note says not to assert definedness on a filetest until
it closes; the same caution applies to asserting `$!` after one until this
closes.

FIX SHAPE (untried): the `p--*` filetest family calls into the same stat path
`stat` uses, which already sets `$!` correctly for a missing path -- so the
errno is available and is being dropped on the filetest return path rather
than never computed.  Check whether the filetest wrapper swallows the
condition; and map the CL error for "closed/invalid stream" onto EBADF rather
than letting it fall through to the ENOENT default (CLAUDE.md rule 12: a
missing case must not fall through to a plausible default).

=== DONE (s470bs) ===

SHIPPED in commit "perl's ERRNO for the whole stat/filetest family" (runtime
only).  Both facts the task named, plus a third the probes found:

  (a) a FILETEST now sets $! â EBADF for a handle that is not open, the
      syscall's own errno for a path.  The task's guess was right: the errno
      was available and being DROPPED, in each filetest's own handler-case.
      There is now ONE failure exit (`%p-stat-fail`) and ONE syscall wrapper
      (`%p-stat-try`, reading errno off the POSIX condition rather than the C
      variable, which an intervening allocation can clobber).
  (b) a CLOSED/never-opened handle is EBADF â the resolver's fourth kind,
      :bad.  Covers a bareword, a closed dirhandle and an in-memory
      (PerlIO::scalar) handle; the LEXICAL spelling is the one residue, filed
      as #1233 (`%p-forget-fh` clears the box, deliberately, and #529's
      `fileno` contract depends on that).
  (c) NOT in the task: a pathname holding a NUL byte fails with ENOENT
      ([perl #131895]).  The C layer TRUNCATES it, so `-f "TEST\0-"` answered
      TRUE for the file TEST â three op/filetest.t rows.

`-t` joined the resolver at the same time, with its own two probed failures
(ENOTTY for an open non-tty, EBADF when the operand names no handle).

THE ROWS THE TASK NAMED ARE STILL BEHIND SOMETHING ELSE.  `t/op/stat_errors.t`
is written as `my $res = eval "$op $arg"` over BAREWORD handles, and inside a
string eval there is no `open` to teach the compiler, so every one of those
barewords is emitted as `(pl-NEVEROPENED)` and DIES before the runtime is
reached.  Filed as **#1231** with the measurement; it is #1044's predicate.

Guard rows 45-57 of `Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t`, inverse-verified (all 13
differ on 027ba9c's runtime).


=== AMENDED (s470bs-merge, 2026-09-06): the owed legs, and one exposed SKIP ===
COMPANION, measured on the finished tree AND on a `git archive 48d8e39`
extraction of main (which reproduces the old numbers exactly, so the move is
this batch's and not BR's or BP's):
  op/stat_errors.t  C 305/333 -> C 510/128  (+205 rows, every one an
                    `error from -X <operand>` assertion).  The s470bs STOP.md
                    predicted NO change here because of #1231 -- the
                    prediction was wrong by 205 rows: #1231 only blocks the
                    BAREWORD operands, and every other operand was reachable.
  op/filetest.t     C 180/254 -> C 369/65   (+189, shared with #1031/#1047/#1048)
ROW DIFF 0 NEW / 394 FIXED / 0 LOST; SHORTFALL 120 = base.

SWEEP: GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed, drops 5 = census, TOTAL 18644 -> 18645.

ONE EXPOSED SKIP, filed as #1237.  perl-tests/readline.t rows 12/13 are gated
on `open F, '.' and binmode F and sysread F, $_, 1; my $err = $! + 0;` and
used to SKIP because `$err` was 0.  This task makes the file's BEGIN block
`-d 't'` leave ENOENT behind exactly as perl does, so `$err` is 2, the SKIP
stops firing, and the rows run -- and fail on the half PCL still lacks: a read
from a DIRECTORY handle sets no errno where perl sets EISDIR (21).  23/5/4 ->
23/7/2, measured serially on both trees.  Blessed in fail-baseline.tsv with
#1237 as the cause; row-shortfall.tsv 8 -> 6.
